h: Views From Old Pale and Days in Chester
p: Once you're back on the ground, the best little detour at Delamere is a walk up to Old Pale. It's a fine high point, and on a clear day you can see across the Cheshire Plain and out towards Wales. It's not a huge climb, which makes it a good one for families with tired legs after the ropes.

Delamere is also on the route of the Sandstone Trail, the long-distance path that runs along Cheshire's sandstone ridge. Keen walkers can tackle a stretch of it, and further south along the ridge, Beeston Castle sits on its rocky crag with views that are well worth the climb.

Timing for the treetops: allow a couple of hours, and give yourselves breathing space before your slot. The forest gets busy on fine weekends, so arriving early takes the stress out of parking. Pack a drink for afterwards, and keep a spare pair of socks in the car if it's been raining, because the forest paths can turn squelchy.

Chester is close by and makes a brilliant partner for a Delamere day, with its Roman walls, the black-and-white Rows and a racecourse right by the river. Chester Zoo, one of the UK's best-known zoos, is just north of the city, so you could easily turn a treetop morning into a full Cheshire weekend.
